#!/bin/bash
# Compare compiled models with the baseline snapshot. Prints, per changed file, the diff lines that are NOT require lines.
REPO="D:/SEM-2/574/Project/audiobookshelf-po"
BASE="$1"
for f in "$REPO"/dist-server/server/models/*.js; do
  n=$(basename "$f")
  if [ ! -f "$BASE/$n" ]; then echo "NEW FILE (not in baseline): $n"; continue; fi
  if cmp -s "$BASE/$n" "$f"; then continue; fi
  d=$(diff "$BASE/$n" "$f" | grep -E '^[<>]')
  total=$(echo "$d" | wc -l)
  other=$(echo "$d" | grep -vE 'require\(|^> const \{[^}]*\} = [A-Za-z_]+;$|^> const [A-Za-z_0-9]+ = [A-Za-z_0-9]+\.[A-Za-z_0-9]+;$')
  if [ -z "$other" ]; then echo "OK   $n: $total changed lines, all require lines"; else echo "DIFF $n: $total changed lines, non-require lines:"; echo "$other" | sed 's/^/       /'; fi
done
for f in "$BASE"/*.js; do n=$(basename "$f"); [ -f "$REPO/dist-server/server/models/$n" ] || echo "MISSING from current: $n"; done

# Scan converted models: banned tokens and counts of !, index signatures, casts, registry declarations, overloads.
REPO="D:/SEM-2/574/Project/audiobookshelf-po"
cd "$REPO"
for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "(no file) $f"; continue; }
  code=$(grep -nvE '^\s*(\*|/\*\*|//)' "$f")
  banned=$(echo "$code" | grep -nE '(:|<|\(|,|\||&|=) *any\b|\bany\[\]|as any|@ts-ignore|@ts-nocheck|@ts-expect-error|as unknown as' | head -5)
  bang=$(echo "$code" | grep -E '[A-Za-z0-9_\)\]]!([\.\)\],;\[ ]|$)' | grep -vE '!==|!= ' | wc -l)
  idx=$(echo "$code" | grep -cE '\[[A-Za-z_]+: string\]:')
  cast=$(echo "$code" | grep -E '[\)\]A-Za-z0-9_\}'"'"'"] as [A-Za-z\{\(\[]' | grep -vE '^\s*[0-9]+:\s*import ' | wc -l)
  reg=$(grep -cE 'declare (static )?readonly sequelize' "$f")
  ovl=$(grep -c 'static init(this: never, ...args: never\[\]): never' "$f")
  exp=$(grep -c '^export = ' "$f")
  echo "$(basename $f): bang=$bang idx=$idx cast=$cast registryDecl=$reg uncallable=$ovl exportEq=$exp ${banned:+BANNED: $banned}"
done

624

626	    const mediaExpanded = this.media || (await this.getMediaExpanded())
627	
628	    let jsonObject = {}
629	    if (this.mediaType === 'book') {
630	      jsonObject = {
631	        tags: mediaExpanded.tags || [],

633	        title: mediaExpanded.title,

641	        }),
642	        genres: mediaExpanded.genres || [],
643	        publishedYear: mediaExpanded.publishedYear,
644	        publishedDate: mediaExpanded.publishedDate,

651	        abridged: !!mediaExpanded.abridged
652	      }
653	    } else {
654	      jsonObject = {
655	        tags: mediaExpanded.tags || [],
656	        title: mediaExpanded.title,
657	        author: mediaExpanded.author,
658	        description: mediaExpanded.description,

673	    return fsExtra
674	      .writeFile(metadataFilePath, JSON.stringify(jsonObject, null, 2))
675	      .then(async () => {

677	        let metadataLibraryFile = this.libraryFiles.find((lf) => lf.metadata.path === filePathToPOSIX(metadataFilePath))
678	        if (storeMetadataWithItem) {

682	            metadataLibraryFile = newLibraryFile.toJSON()

686	            if (fileTimestamps) {

688	              metadataLibraryFile.metadata.ctimeMs = fileTimestamps.ctimeMs
689	              metadataLibraryFile.metadata.size = fileTimestamps.size

699	            this.size = size

The last check (16:26:42, after my last edit) shows no errors in my three files and none in other files naming my models. I did not run the build or the tests.

A single-file `ts.transpileModule` of each converted file, written to the scratchpad only (not a tsc run), was diffed against your `baseline-models` copies. Only the require lines differ, plus the three cast comments listed below. Every original require is still emitted.

## Counts per converted model
| Model | `!` | Index signatures | `as` casts | Registry declarations (B.2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BookSeries | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| BookAuthor | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Book | 0 | 0 | 2 | 1 (instance side only) |

No `import type` replaces a require in any of the three, so there is nothing to name in the commit message.

### BookSeries.ts
- `sequence` is `string | null`: the column is nullable and `Book.updateSeriesFromRequest()` stores null.
- `removeByIds(seriesId: string | null = null, bookId: string | null = null)`, with `where` typed `{ seriesId?: string; bookId?: string }`.
- init overloads are at lines 36-37, the implementation at line 42.

### BookAuthor.ts
- **Cast, line 63:** `}) as (BookAuthor & { count: number })[]`. With `raw: true` the rows carry the `COUNT` alias, which Sequelize's `findAll` typing does not know. The comment shows in the compiled file.
- `getCountsForAuthors` has an explicit return type `Promise<Record<string, number>>`.
- init overloads are at lines 73-74, the implementation at line 79.

### Book.ts
- **Registry declaration, line 181** (type at line 23): `declare readonly sequelize: Sequelize & { models: RegisteredModels }` with entries author, bookAuthor, series, bookSeries. Book has no static registry reads, so there is no static declaration.
- **Cast, line 428:** `structuredClone(af) as AudioTrack` in `getTracklist()`.
  - This is not an untyped-module boundary, so it stretches rule 5.
  - The alternative without a cast is `const track: AudioFileObject & Partial<Book.AudioTrackProperties> = structuredClone(af)`. It makes `getTracklist()` return tracks whose title, contentUrl and startOffset are optional for every consumer.
  - I kept the cast; say if you want the swap.
- **Cast, line 656:** `await seriesModel.findOrCreateByNameAndLibrary(...) as SeriesExpanded`. The Series model returns a plain Series, and the next line attaches `bookSeries`.
- **Namespace, line 26:** `declare namespace Book` exports the typedef names as real types, plus a new `FileMetadataObject`. Other agents' files already read them: `Author.ts:8`, `PodcastEpisode.ts:6-7`, `Series.ts:8`.
- **Nullable fields** that differ from the constructor JSDoc:
  - The nine string columns (title, subtitle, publishedYear, publishedDate, publisher, description, isbn, asin, language) are `string | null`, because `updateFromRequest()` writes `payload.metadata[key] || null` to all nine. They must share one type for the `this[key] = ...` write to check.
  - `coverPath` is `string | null` (`BookScanner.js:151` and `LibraryItemController.js:379` set null).
  - `ebookFile` is `EBookFileObject | null`.
- **Other type decisions:**
  - `series` is `SeriesExpanded[]` and `SeriesExpandedProperties.bookSeries` is the BookSeries model, because the code calls `.save()` on it.
  - `AudioFileObject` gains `exclude: boolean`, which `includedAudioFiles` reads and the JSDoc typedef lacks.
  - `metaTags` is `ReturnType<AudioMetaTags['toJSON']>`.
- **No index signature for the dynamic keys.** The key arrays are annotated instead (`MetadataStringKey[]` at line 508, `('narrators' | 'genres')[]` at line 541).
- **Payload type, line 107:** `BookUpdatePayload` is a union, `{ metadata: ...; tags?: unknown } | { metadata?: undefined; tags?: unknown }`. That lets `if (payload.metadata)` narrow `payload` itself, which also holds inside the `forEach` callbacks.
- **utils annotation, lines 6-10:** the two helpers are annotated with method signatures taking `string | null`. Their JSDoc says `string`, but `getTitleParts()` handles a missing title. I chose method syntax for its bivariant parameter check and did not test the arrow form.
- `oldMetadataToJSONExpanded()` uses a draft type (line 110) for its local, so the six added keys are optional in its return type.
- init overloads are at lines 266-267, the implementation at line 272.

## LibraryItem: why it is skipped
I prepared a first typing pass outside the repo, put it in the repo for one check (16:24:15 to 16:24:42), then restored it.

1. **Rule D blocker.** `Book` and `Podcast` are required at `LibraryItem.js:8-9` but never used as values, only in JSDoc. TypeScript drops both requires from the output; the scratch transpile confirms it. This needs your decision; I invented no workaround.
2. **81 compiler errors after the first pass.** Original line numbers:
   - **96, 152, 243:** `where`, `replacements` and `include` default to null, which Sequelize's typings reject (TS2322, TS2769).
   - **174:** `include` given as an object where the typings want an array (TS2353).
   - **302-321:** properties that `libraryFilters` attaches (collapsedSeries, series, rssFeed, numEpisodesIncomplete, mediaItemShare, media.numEpisodes), read from `li` and added to the `toOldJSONMinified()` result (TS2339, 18 errors).
   - **353:** five arguments to a four-parameter function (TS2554).
   - **355-356, 632-669, 924-926:** `media` is `Book | Podcast` and the code branches on `mediaType`, which narrows nothing (TS2339, TS2551, TS18046). Each kind-specific read would need a cast.
   - **385-387, 494, then 395-522:** `timed()` loaders (TS2739, then 22 TS18046). This comes from my probe's `loader` type and is probably fixable.
   - **568:** `user` null passed to a `User` parameter (TS2345).
   - **674:** `fsExtra.writeFile` (the known pitfall).
   - **682-683:** `LibraryFile.toJSON()` is not assignable to `LibraryFileObject`.
   - **695-696:** numbers assigned to the Date fields `mtime` and `ctime` (TS2322).
   - **708:** untyped `.catch` parameter (TS7006).
   - **819-820, 838:** the `afterFind` and `afterDestroy` hooks: reassigned `findResult`, and `instance` typed as a plain Model.
   - **873:** `this[mixinMethodName](options)` (TS7053).
   - **943:** optional `episodeId` passed on (TS2345).
3. Part of the `media` noise comes from Podcast's class index signature (`Podcast.ts:67`, sub-agent 3). It turns Book-only reads on `Book | Podcast` into `unknown`.

## Errors in other files tied to my models
- `server/models/MediaItemShare.ts(145,92): error TS2345: Argument of type 'null' is not assignable to parameter of type 'BindOrReplacements | undefined'.`
  - It is the call `libraryItemModel.findOneExpanded({ mediaId }, null, {...})`. The JSDoc at `LibraryItem.js:238` types `replacements` as optional, not nullable.
  - It stays while LibraryItem is JavaScript. Your second grep does not catch it, because the message does not name LibraryItem.
- There are no "waiting on <Model>" errors in my files.

## Declarations needed in server/types/
None.

## Bugs and oddities found, not fixed
- **Book typedef `EBookFileObject`** (JSDoc, originally `Book.js:15`): `relPath:strFing` is a typo.
- **Book typedef `AudioFileObject`:** it lacks `exclude`, which `AudioFile.toJSON()` stores and `includedAudioFiles` reads.
- **`Book.js:441` and `:496`:** `updateAuthorsFromRequest` and `updateSeriesFromRequest` return null for invalid input; their JSDoc promises an object.
- **`Book.js:517-519` and `:552`:** `bookSeries.sequence` is read without the `?.` guard that lines 253 and 348 use.
- **`Book.js:392`:** a request with an empty or null title sets `title` to null; nothing validates it.
- **`LibraryItem.js:353`:** `getMediaItemsInProgress(library, user, include, limit, false)` passes a fifth argument that `libraryFilters.js:56` ignores.
- **`LibraryItem.js:695-696`:** `mtimeMs` and `ctimeMs` numbers are assigned to fields documented as Date.
- **`LibraryItem.js:8-9`:** two requires whose bindings are never used.
